↳ Posted by ryaners1 on October 16th, 2002.

Yes please

This is one of my favorite tunes to play. Again I gave no ornaments, I figure that cam come later in discussion. Anyway I learned this as “Do You Want Anymore” and play it on (gasp!) the recorder, ’cause it’s just so much fun, & makes me look like I’m playing faster than I am. :) I didn’t know there was another name for it until I heard Cillian & Niall Vallely play it in concert as a reel… the Collier’s Reel. Niall swears a lot of people play it but he can’t remember who. Both versions are great. I’ve noticed that all the copies I can find online are very different from what we play, so I thought I’d share this way.

Cheers!
Trinil

↳ Posted by Trinil on October 16th, 2002.

↳ Posted by Connor Hickey on May 9th, 2019.

Re: Do You Want Any More?

On the Kane sisters’ debut album (The Well-Tempered Bow, which oddly isn’t the name of a tune on the album, lol), they close the record with “Do You Want Anymore?”, into The Broken Pledge in jig form, into the reel Maude Miller… Played with their perfect,signature steady tempo, strong bowing, and the perfect blend of repetition & ornaments/variations. It’s fun how they play Collier’s as a jig followed by Broken Pledge as well.

TBH, I learned the BP and Colliers jigs when I was in high school, before ever knowing of either reel! It took me traveling to Limerick, to one of the nightly sessions at Dolan’s Warehouse, where I was amazed at these reels. The shock. The awe of it all. My friends says, “Ah sure, it’s called The Colliers reel. Class tune; fairly common, though, loike.”

↳ Posted by Erik-Fiddler on September 29th, 2022.

Re: Do You Want Any More?

This melody beautifully insists on the c

and the mode hesitates between mixolydian and ionian.

The whistle and ‘fretless flute’ offer a wide range of c’s from c natural to c sharp; this well-loved tune provides a good workout for your c’s on your fretless instruments.
